purpose: Select an equivalent target T-CONT queue during GEM rebinding, matching the original scheduling policy and SP priority or WRR weight.
root_cause: When the requested GEM queue owner differs from the CTP target T-CONT, native update_queue_bindings chose the first configured queue on the target T-CONT. The shipped original scans for the same scheduling-policy flag and the same saved SP priority or WRR weight, retaining the requested queue if no equivalent exists. Choosing a different queue can merge independently scheduled GEMs or give a GEM the wrong priority/weight.
concrete_example: Requested SP queue0 has priority5 on T-CONT0. Target T-CONT1 has queue1 priority6 and queue2 priority5. Old native chose queue1; original chooses queue2. For target priorities6/4 with no equivalent, original retains queue0; old native still chose queue1.
fix: Resolve each queue scheduling policy from its referenced scheduler or RelatedPort T-CONT.
Require policy equality and matching SP priority or WRR weight during the existing target-owner fallback scan.
Retain the requested queue when no equivalent target queue exists, following the original scan.
Correct the pre-existing regression assertion that expected different-priority queues to be interchangeable.

verification.stock_cases: Actual original scan: SP skips different priority; SP skips WRR with same numeric value; WRR skips different weight; no match retains requested queue.
verification.stock_scope: Actual shipped scan and ME-ID selection instructions with synthetic active queue rows. No function callbacks or reimplemented scan; MIB construction, ioctl, queue programming and optics outside scope.
verification.before_result: New SP fallback regression failed on the production pre-fix Rust library because GEM0 shared the wrong queue with GEM1. The first failure aborts the test; no claim that all cases ran before the fix.
verification.after_result: Existing OMCI queue FFI regression passes, including four added scenarios: SP/WRR with an equivalent target queue and with no equivalent. Existing remap, weight, backend-error rollback and invalid-pointer checks also pass.
verification.native_scope: Real baseline OMCI requests through the production Rust FFI and snapshot exporter; apply callback captures the actual payload and models hardware success/failure. Does not program the physical PUC or simulate OLT timing.
verification.build_scope: Offline locked Cargo builds of the OMCI static library only, including cortex-a55 aarch64-unknown-linux-musl target. Isolated target directory; no full firmware build or test suite.

limits: Queue-selection defect is reproduced and corrected offline. It does not establish the cause of the reported -110 table timeout or approximately50-second ACTP reset.
The queue matching comparison uses MIB policy/priority/weight; complete equivalence of all original queue database lifecycle states is not claimed.
No physical XGPON OLT test, firmware deployment, commit or push.
